outputCopy.heroIntroduction: Residents in Thurnscoe can access NHS Pharmacy First services through Yorkshire Pharmacy & Health Clinic. This service allows local people to consult a trained pharmacist for a range of common health conditions, supporting the community with professional advice and clinical assessments tailored to individual health needs.
outputCopy.localIntroduction:
Thurnscoe is a former coal mining village situated within the Dearne Valley in the Metropolitan Borough of Barnsley, South Yorkshire. Deeply rooted in the region's industrial past, the settlement grew significantly during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries around Hickleton Main Colliery. Today, it operates primarily as a residential area while maintaining strong connections to its surrounding landscape and local heritage.

The village offers access to several public open spaces, most notably Phoenix Park, which was developed on the restored ground of the former colliery, alongside Thurnscoe Park. Essential services and local retail outlets are focused along Houghton Road and Station Road, providing everyday amenities for residents. The neighbourhood is served by Thurnscoe railway station on the Wakefield line, alongside local healthcare provision such as GP practices serving the immediate population.

To help address local healthcare requirements, Yorkshire Pharmacy & Health Clinic provides Pharmacy First consultations for eligible people from the area. Pharmacy First covers certain common health conditions, offering an accessible route for clinical support. During a consultation, the pharmacist assesses symptoms, relevant medicines and medical history. Depending on the individual clinical assessment, the outcome may include self-care advice, suitable treatment or referral to another healthcare professional, as eligibility and treatment vary by patient.
outputCopy.relationshipToPharmacy: Consultations take place at Yorkshire Pharmacy & Health Clinic in Darfield. Yorkshire Pharmacy & Health Clinic is approximately 4.9 km in a straight line from Thurnscoe.
